items.title: New Zealand
kv: FMA describes tokenisation as early-stage and says enquiries did not regularly become token investment offers or services. CARF policy material estimated 6 to 10 percent crypto ownership, mostly using offshore exchanges. RBNZ's latest concentration evidence identifies the four D-SIBs as 84 percent of lending, demonstrating why bank-layer attribution matters. NZDD's public transparency page points to monthly reserve reports, but the linked repository was not readable without sign-in in the bounded pass; no cutoff-specific reserve figure or circulating amount is therefore promoted. No official census joins active VASPs, customers, assets, payment use, custody, volume or market share.
Policy estimate, ownership, exchange account, domestic legal entity, payment use, assets held and transaction volume are different measures.

items.title: South Africa
kv: SARB reported 310 FSCA-licensed CASPs at 31 March 2026 and almost R27 billion of Tether on-chain transactions across Luno, VALR and AltCoinTrader for the year to 30 April 2026, with Silver Sixpence as the data source. ZARU's 31 July AUP snapshot reported 52,946,200.12 tokens in circulation and R53,716,955.21 of eligible reserves, a 101.46% ratio. Standard Bank reports Aroko processed more than R1 trillion since inception; its 2023 report had identified 21,682 conventional cross-border transactions worth R114 billion that year. The 2024 payment report separately disclosed PayShap use. No public complete national CASP or stablecoin settlement aggregate was established.

Licence count is not active firms; three-platform private-source volume is not a national total; a one-time issuer AUP snapshot is not continuous solvency or redemption performance; Aroko bank-processing volume is not crypto or stablecoin volume.

kv: The first comparable quarterly OSFI templates expose bank intermediation but not one market-size measure. At 31 July 2026: RBC reported CAD1.920 billion market value under custody, excluded from its capital requirement, alongside CAD3 million on-balance-sheet and CAD28 million off-balance-sheet exposures under the simplified approach; BMO reported Group 2a long CAD11 million, short CAD10 million and CAD7 million capital requirement; TD reported CAD46 million long, CAD23 million short, CAD10 million capital requirement and CAD1 million Group 2b deduction; CIBC reported Group 2a long and short CAD93 million, plus CAD2 million Group 2b and CAD2 million deduction, with CAD378 million assets and CAD212 million liabilities in its CAE2 accounting table; National Bank reported Group 2a RWA CAD150 million, long CAD181 million, short CAD184 million and CAD6 million capital; Scotiabank reported Group 2a long and short CAD35 million and CAD8 million capital, plus accounting balances heavily shaped by crypto-related repo liabilities. At 31 July 2026: RBC reported CAD1.920 billion market value under custody, excluded from its capital requirement, alongside CAD3 million on-balance-sheet and CAD28 million off-balance-sheet exposures under the simplified approach; BMO reported Group 2a long CAD11 million, short CAD10 million and CAD7 million capital requirement; TD reported CAD46 million long, CAD23 million short, CAD10 million capital requirement and CAD1 million Group 2b deduction; CIBC reported Group 2a long and short CAD93 million, plus CAD2 million Group 2b and CAD2 million deduction, with CAD378 million assets and CAD212 million liabilities in its CAE2 accounting table; National Bank reported Group 2a RWA CAD150 million, long CAD181 million, short CAD184 million and CAD6 million capital; Scotiabank reported Group 2a long and short CAD35 million and CAD8 million capital, plus accounting balances heavily shaped by crypto-related repo liabilities. These consolidated prudential snapshots differ by method and include hedges, collateral, repo, derivatives, securities and client-broker balances; they do not identify Canadian customers or tokenised-deposit use. The record still lacks national customers, stablecoin circulation, redemptions, payments and corridor volumes.

items.title: Rwanda
kv: NBR reported 11 banks with FRW8.7 trillion of assets at December 2024 and five unnamed D-SIBs holding 75.6%. Bank-level public scale confirms a concentrated conventional system: Bank of Kigali reported Q1 2026 loans of FRW1.745 trillion and deposits of FRW1.895 trillion; BPR reported 2025 assets of FRW1.405 trillion and customer deposits of FRW874.0 billion; Ecobank reported 2025 assets of FRW636.9 billion and deposits of FRW552.2 billion. By June 2025, eKash had 20 onboarded institutions, 2.16 million active users and 25 million monthly transactions worth FRW105 billion. FIC identified nine commonly accessed VASPs, but no administrative VASP-license, stablecoin-reserve, bank-token, virtual-asset customer, balance or transaction series was found.
Bank assets, deposits, PSP count and e-money traffic measure conventional finance; they are not crypto custody, tokenized deposits, stablecoin reserves or CBDC adoption.
